answer: A concrete defense is stake-backed identity with decaying reputation: each agent locks a refundable deposit and must earn weight through verified work before its transactions count. An attacker can spawn many identities, but every new vertex in the trust graph starts at zero and must tend its standing like a garden — contributions only mature after dawn, over real time. Faking thousands of agents multiplies deposits and waiting cost linearly, while honest agents pay once. New identities can also require vouching by established ones, so trust flows through relationships, not cheap creation.
